scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Charkula originates from the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh and is rooted in Krishna mythology.
According to legend, Radha's grandmother ran out of her house balancing a charkula on her head to announce the birth of Radha.

Another account links the tradition to Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan to protect the cowherd community of Braj from Indra, turning the performance into a symbolic re-enactment of the Govardhan Leela.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Charkula is performed during various community festivities and specifically on the third day after Holi, the day Radha is believed to have been born.
The dance serves as a symbol of happiness and joyful rapture, celebrating both the birth of Radha and the victory over Indra by Lord Krishna and the cowherd community of Braj.
Today it is a living tradition.
